articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to guarantee the basic living of unemployed persons during unemployment and to promote their re-employment.

Article 2 Urban enterprises and institutions and their employees shall pay unemployment insurance premiums in accordance with these Regulations.
Unemployed persons of urban enterprises and institutions shall enjoy unemployment insurance benefits in accordance with these Regulations.
For the purpose of this Article, "urban enterprises" means state-owned enterprises, urban collective enterprises, foreign-invested enterprises, urban private enterprises and other urban enterprises.

Article 3 The labor and social security administrative department of the State Council shall be in charge of the unemployment insurance work nationwide. The labor and social security administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of the unemployment insurance work within their respective administrative areas. The social insurance agencies handling unemployment insurance business established by the labor and social security administrative departments according to the provisions of the State Council shall specifically undertake the unemployment insurance work in accordance with these Regulations.
Article 4 Unemployment insurance premiums shall be collected in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 6 Urban enterprises and institutions shall pay unemployment insurance premiums at 2% of their total payroll. Employees of urban enterprises and institutions shall pay unemployment insurance premiums at 1% of their own wages. Peasant contract workers employed by urban enterprises and institutions shall not pay unemployment insurance premiums themselves.

Article 7 The unemployment insurance fund shall be subject to overall planning at the municipal level in municipalities directly under the Central Government and cities with districts; the level of overall planning in other areas shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions.

Article 8 Provinces and autonomous regions may establish unemployment insurance adjustment funds.
The unemployment insurance adjustment fund shall be raised based on the unemployment insurance premiums that shall be collected according to law in the overall planning areas, in proportion prescribed by the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions.
Where the unemployment insurance fund in an overall planning area is insufficient, it shall be adjusted by the unemployment insurance adjustment fund and subsidized by local finance.
The specific measures for raising and adjusting the use of the unemployment insurance adjustment fund and local financial subsidies shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions.

Article 9 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, subject to approval by the State Council, appropriately adjust the rate of unemployment insurance premiums in their respective administrative areas based on the number of unemployed persons and the amount of unemployment insurance fund in those areas.

Article 11 The unemployment insurance fund must be deposited into the financial special account for social security funds opened by the financial department in state-owned commercial banks, managed with separate revenue and expenditure lines, and supervised by the financial department according to law.
The unemployment insurance fund deposited in banks and used to purchase government bonds according to the provisions of the State shall accrue interest at the deposit interest rates for urban and rural residents for the same period and at the government bond interest rates respectively. The interest on the unemployment insurance fund shall be incorporated into the unemployment insurance fund.
The unemployment insurance fund shall be used for designated purposes only, and shall not be misappropriated for other uses or used to balance financial revenue and expenditure.

Article 12 The budget and final accounts of the revenue and expenditure of the unemployment insurance fund shall be prepared by the social insurance agency in the overall planning area, reviewed by the labor and social security administrative department at the same level, verified by the financial department at the same level, and submitted to the people's government at the same level for approval.
Article 13 The financial system and accounting system for the unemployment insurance fund shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 16 Urban enterprises and institutions shall, in a timely manner, issue to unemployed persons a certificate of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship, inform them of their right to enjoy unemployment insurance benefits according to regulations, and report the list of unemployed persons to the social insurance agency for record within 7 days from the date of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship.
After an employee of an urban enterprise or institution becomes unemployed, he/she shall, holding the certificate of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship issued by the employer, register as unemployed at the designated social insurance agency in a timely manner. The unemployment insurance benefits shall be calculated from the date of registration as unemployed.
The unemployment insurance benefits shall be paid monthly by the social insurance agency. The social insurance agency shall issue to the unemployed person a document for receiving unemployment insurance benefits, and the unemployed person shall present such document to the designated bank to receive the benefits.

Article 17 Where the cumulative contribution period of the unemployed person's former employer and the person himself/herself according to regulations is between one year and less than five years, the maximum period for receiving unemployment insurance benefits shall be 12 months; where the cumulative contribution period is between five years and less than ten years, the maximum period shall be 18 months; where the cumulative contribution period is ten years or more, the maximum period shall be 24 months. After re-employment, if the person becomes unemployed again, the contribution period shall be recalculated, and the period for receiving unemployment insurance benefits may be combined with the period that was entitled but not yet received for the previous unemployment, provided that the combined period shall not exceed 24 months.

Article 18 The standard of unemployment insurance benefits shall be determined by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government at a level lower than the local minimum wage standard and higher than the minimum living security standard for urban residents.

Article 19 Where an unemployed person falls ill and seeks medical treatment during the period of receiving unemployment insurance benefits, he/she may apply to the social insurance agency for medical subsidies according to regulations. The standard of medical subsidies shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 20 Where an unemployed person dies during the period of receiving unemployment insurance benefits, a one-time funeral subsidy and pension shall be paid to his/her family members by reference to the provisions on in-service employees of the locality.

Article 21 Where a peasant contract worker employed by an employer has worked continuously for a full year, and the employer has paid unemployment insurance premiums, and the labor contract expires without renewal or is prematurely dissolved, the social insurance agency shall pay a one-time living subsidy to him/her based on the length of his/her working period. The methods and standards of the subsidy shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 22 Where an urban enterprise or institution is transferred as a whole across overall planning areas, or an unemployed person moves across overall planning areas, the unemployment insurance relationship shall be transferred accordingly.

Article 23 Where an unemployed person meets the conditions for minimum living security for urban residents, he/she shall enjoy the treatment of minimum living security for urban residents according to regulations.
Article 26 The financial department and the audit department shall supervise the revenue, expenditure and management of the unemployment insurance fund according to law.
Article 27 The necessary expenses of the social insurance agency shall be included in the budget and allocated by finance.

Article 28 Where a person who does not meet the conditions for enjoying unemployment insurance benefits fraudulently obtains unemployment insurance benefits and other unemployment insurance benefits, the social insurance agency shall order him/her to return the amounts; if the circumstances are serious, the labor and social security administrative department shall impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the amount fraudulently obtained.

Article 29 Where a staff member of a social insurance agency, in violation of regulations, issues to an unemployed person documents for receiving unemployment insurance benefits or enjoying other unemployment insurance benefits, causing losses to the unemployment insurance fund, the labor and social security administrative department shall order the recovery of the losses; if the circumstances are serious, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law.

Article 30 Where a staff member of the labor and social security administrative department or a social insurance agency abuses his/her power, engages in malpractices for personal gain, or neglects his/her duties, causing losses to the unemployment insurance fund, the labor and social security administrative department shall recover the lost unemployment insurance fund; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law.

Article 31 Where any unit or individual misappropriates the unemployment insurance fund, the misappropriated fund shall be recovered; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated and incorporated into the unemployment insurance fund; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons.

Article 32 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in light of the actual local circumstances, decide that these Regulations shall apply to social organizations and their full-time staff, private non-enterprise units and their employees, and urban individual industrial and commercial households with employees and their employees within their respective administrative areas.

Article 33 These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. The Provisions on Unemployment Insurance for Employees of State-owned Enterprises promulgated by the State Council on April 12, 1993 shall be abolished simultaneously.
